title: dedicated-autoscaler: integrate burst controls with fleet SLO and utilization reporting
author: Maya Patel
ci_status: pass (one flaky integration test was rerun and passed)
body:
Motivation: We observed two recurring problems in dedicated fleets during high burst traffic: (1) transient burst requests bypassing the token-bucket controls caused short-lived overloads and tail-latency spikes; (2) utilization and SLO reporting were not correlated with burst throttling behavior, making post-incident analysis slow. This PR ties burst controls into the fleet autoscaler control loop and improves utilization/SLO reporting so operators can reason about burst consumption versus steady throughput.

What I changed: consolidated the token-bucket burst controller into the FleetAutoscaler (services/dedicated-autoscaler), added smoothing parameters and an adaptive backpressure signal for the scheduler, and emitted new metrics for burst_consumed_tokens, burst_allowed_rate, burst_rejected_count, and fleet_burst_utilization. Updated the metrics schema and dashboards to reflect burst vs steady capacity. Added a config flag `enable_burst_integration` (false by default) to allow gradual rollout.

Key behavioral changes:
- Burst token accounting is now global per-fleet and accounted against SLO-aware throughput guarantees.
- Autoscaler uses a smoothed estimate of burst usage to adjust temporary capacity allowances, reducing oscillation.
- Requests rejected by burst controls now emit structured logs with route/model tags to help triage.
- Utilization reporting separates burst-adjusted utilization vs steady-utilization so we can attribute cost and latency.

Testing: unit tests for token-bucket math and backpressure logic, integration test that simulates burst traffic patterns across three fleets with different SLOs, and e2e canary run in staging. One flaky integration test (TestFleetAutoscalerBackpressure) was rerun; both runs passed.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind `enable_burst_integration`. Will enable in staging for 48h monitoring, then opt-in one small customer fleet, then gradual percent rollout using canary percentages in the fleet-config. Dashboard panels and alerting adjustments included in this PR to detect regressions (increased rejection rates or unexpected capacity churn).

Related: ENG-21400 (autoscaler smoothing), ENG-21510 (SLO-backed throughput guarantees), SUP-8921 incident follow-up.
commits: Add burst token accounting and global token-bucket integration into FleetAutoscaler
Add smoothing + adaptive backpressure signal to scheduler
Emit new burst and utilization metrics; update metrics schema v3
Add unit tests and integration test harness for burst scenarios
Add dashboards and alerting updates; docs for feature flag rollout
review_comments: Lucas Nguyen (review): Left small comments on backpressure damping constants — prefer named constants and a short comment explaining rationale. Also suggested adding a histogram for burst token latency.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed Lucas comments, moved magic numbers to constants and added histogram for token allocation latency. Added a short comment linking to ENG-21400 notes.
Priya Sharma (review): Can we make the default smoothing half-life configurable without a restart? Concerned about operational flexibility.
Maya Patel (author): Added dynamic smoothing config exposed through runtime-config; updated docs and tests.
release_notes: Added optional integration between burst controls and fleet autoscaler. New metrics: burst_consumed_tokens, burst_allowed_rate, burst_rejected_count, fleet_burst_utilization. Feature is feature-gated and off by default. Improves stability under transient burst load and gives operators clearer reporting.
additional_notes: Canary rollout tracked in Linear ENG-21400. Ops runbook included. No API breaking changes; only adds new metrics and a feature flag.
